goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed content is persisted as raw HTML without sanitization, so a compromised feed can inject same-origin stored XSS into every embed viewer.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, the code creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In app/models/post.rb, when cook_method is :raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any processing: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from ruby-readability parsing. In the view app/views/embed/best.html.erb, the cooked content is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` which outputs it without escaping. Since the raw HTML from external sources is stored and rendered without sanitization, a malicious feed could inject JavaScript that would execute in the context of the Discourse domain when users view the embedded content. This is a real stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — One malformed feed item (for example a missing content field) aborts the entire non-retrying poll, allowing an early bad item to indefinitely block all later article updates.
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 — Removing the public `--category` option breaks existing import scripts and silently drops callers' category selection.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the `method_option :category` line is removed (line 117 in the old file), and the code that used `options[:category]` to set `category_id` is also removed. The import method now uses `TopicEmbed.import_remote` instead of `PostCreator.new` with a category parameter. This is a real breaking change - existing scripts that pass `--category` or `-c` will have that option silently ignored, and posts will no longer be created in the specified category. This is a backwards-incompatible change to a public CLI interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The embed API concatenates `discourseUrl` without normalizing a trailing slash, so a valid base URL like `https://forum.example.com` produces a broken endpoint URL.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 7: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com' (without trailing slash), the result would be 'https://forum.example.comembed/best?...' which is indeed a broken URL. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com/' (with trailing slash), it would work correctly as 'https://forum.example.com/embed/best?...'. The code does not normalize the trailing slash, so this is a real bug that could cause the embed functionality to fail depending on how discourseUrl is configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Root-relative rewriting corrupts scheme-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png by treating the CDN hostname as a path on the article host.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 53-70, the absolutize_urls method checks if href/src start_with?('/') and then prepends the prefix. However, scheme-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/image.png' also start with '/', so they would be incorrectly transformed to something like 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.png'. The code does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` which strips leading slashes, but this still results in corruption because '//cdn.example.com/image.png' becomes 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.png' instead of preserving the original scheme-relative URL. This is a real bug that would corrupt valid scheme-relative URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — Relative links without a leading slash are never resolved against the article URL, so imported links and images can point at the Discourse host instead of the source page.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code only handles URLs that start with '/': `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')`. Relative URLs without a leading slash (like 'images/wat.jpg' or 'hello.html') would not be matched by this condition and would remain as relative URLs. When rendered in Discourse, these relative URLs would resolve against the Discourse domain rather than the original source domain. This is a real bug - the code handles absolute-path URLs (/path) but not relative URLs (path) which are also valid and common in HTML content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — Feed items without a content field raise on nil.scrub instead of falling back to description or skipping the item, aborting the entire poll.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:1 — Populating an existing previously empty migration means deployments that already recorded this version will never create topic_embeds.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that the migration file 'db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb' is 'populating an existing previously empty migration'. However, looking at the diff, this file is being created as a NEW file (indicated by 'new file mode' in the diff header). The file creates the topic_embeds table with proper columns and an index. This is a standard new migration file, not a modification to an existing empty migration. The finding appears to be a misreading of the diff - there's no evidence this migration existed before in an empty state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:1 — Populating an existing previously empty migration means deployments that already recorded this version will never add posts.cook_method, causing runtime SQL failures.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims this is 'populating an existing previously empty migration', but looking at the diff, this is a NEW migration file being created (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). The diff shows 'new file mode' and the entire content is being added. This is not modifying an existing migration - it's creating a new one. The migration correctly adds the cook_method column with a default value of 1. There is no issue with deployments that 'already recorded this version' because this is a brand new migration file that hasn't been run anywhere yet.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Adding force: true to table creation can drop an existing top_topics table and its data during migration execution.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to adding 'force: true' to the create_table call in the migration. Looking at the diff, line 3 changes from 'create_table :top_topics do |t|' to 'create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|'. The 'force: true' option in Rails migrations will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. This is a real concern because if this migration is run on a database where the top_topics table already exists with data, that data would be lost. However, this is a migration file - migrations are typically run once in sequence. The concern would be if someone re-runs migrations or if the table was created outside of migrations. While this is a valid observation about potentially destructive behavior, in the context of a new migration being added, this is often intentional to ensure clean table creation. The risk is real but context-dependent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — TopicEmbed mixes remote HTTP extraction and HTML rewriting into the persistence model, tightly coupling network and parsing concerns to database writes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding describes an architectural/design concern about mixing concerns (remote HTTP fetching, HTML parsing, and database persistence) in the TopicEmbed model. Looking at the diff, TopicEmbed.import_remote does fetch remote content via HTTP and process it, while TopicEmbed.import handles persistence. However, this is a design/architecture opinion about code organization and separation of concerns, not a bug, security issue, or correctness problem. The code functions correctly as written. This is a style/architecture nit rather than a real defect that would cause incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key is never called, leaving dead cache-key code and an otherwise unnecessary digest dependency.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, I can see the feed_key method defined at lines 20-22. Searching through the entire diff, this method is never called anywhere - not in poll_feed.rb itself, not in topic_retriever.rb, not in any other file. The method creates a cache key using Digest::SHA1 but is never used. This is indeed dead code that was added but never utilized, which is a real (though minor) code quality issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — The job loads email/sender even though it never references email delivery, creating an unrelated dependency.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb, line 1 shows `require_dependency 'email/sender'`. The job class RetrieveTopic only uses TopicRetriever to retrieve topics and doesn't use any email functionality. This is indeed an unnecessary dependency that adds overhead and creates coupling to unrelated code. However, this is more of a code quality/cleanup issue rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness problem. The code will still function correctly with this extra require. This is essentially a style/cleanup nit rather than a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Every distinct missing embed URL reruns the entire feed poll, causing an unbounded feed download and per-item database/import work that can amplify concurrent requests into severe load.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:41, the perform_retrieve method checks if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? and if so, calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}). This executes the entire feed poll synchronously. The poll_feed method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb downloads the RSS feed and iterates through all items, calling TopicEmbed.import for each. While there is a 60-second throttle via retrieved_recently? for non-staff users, staff users bypass this throttle (@opts[:no_throttle]). For regular users, concurrent requests within the 60-second window would be blocked, but the first request for any new embed URL would trigger a full feed poll. This is a real performance concern - each unique missing embed URL causes a full feed download and processing, which could be exploited or cause load issues with many distinct URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — Remote article retrieval has no open/read timeout, so a stalled origin can occupy a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code uses `open(url).read` from the open-uri library without specifying any timeout options. This is called in `import_remote` method which fetches remote content. The open-uri library by default has no timeout, meaning if a remote server stalls or is slow to respond, the worker thread will block indefinitely. This is a real issue - when this code runs in a Sidekiq job (via TopicRetriever.fetch_http or Jobs::PollFeed), a stalled origin server could tie up a worker indefinitely. This is a legitimate operational/reliability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Feed polling disables retries, so any transient network or parsing failure drops the entire hourly import attempt.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 12 in poll_feed.rb which has `sidekiq_options retry: false`. This is a deliberate design choice, not a bug. The code explicitly disables retries for this scheduled job. While one could argue this is a suboptimal design decision (transient failures won't be retried), this is a design/architecture choice rather than a bug or defect. The job is scheduled to run hourly anyway, so a failed attempt will be retried in the next hour. This is a style/design preference, not a correctness problem or bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — One malformed feed item raises while decoding content and prevents all later valid items in the feed from being imported.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 35 in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. This is inside a loop `rss.items.each do |i|`. If `i.content` is nil or if `scrub` or `CGI.unescapeHTML` raises an exception for a malformed item, the exception would propagate up and stop processing of all remaining items. There's no try/catch or error handling around individual item processing. This is a real bug - one bad feed item would prevent all subsequent items from being imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed-supplied HTML is stored with raw_html cooking and rendered without sanitization, enabling persistent XSS through malicious RSS content.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In app/models/post.rb, when cook_method is :raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any processing. The content comes from RSS feeds (in poll_feed.rb via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from ruby-readability parsing. While ruby-readability does filter to specific tags, the RSS content path doesn't sanitize HTML before storing it. The post is then rendered in views using `raw post.cooked` (in embed/best.html.erb line 18), which outputs unescaped HTML. This creates a persistent XSS vulnerability where malicious RSS content could inject scripts. However, looking more carefully at ruby-readability usage in import_remote, it specifies allowed tags: `tags: %w[div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img]` which excludes script tags. But the poll_feed.rb path uses CGI.unescapeHTML on raw content without sanitization before passing to TopicEmbed.import. This is a real XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open-uri follows redirects without revalidating the destination host or blocking private addresses, allowing an approved embed host to redirect user-triggered fetches into internal services.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code uses `open(url).read` where `url` comes from user input (the embed_url parameter). The `open-uri` library in Ruby does follow HTTP redirects automatically. If an attacker controls a page on an approved embeddable_host, they could set up a redirect to internal services (like http://169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata, or internal network services). The code only validates the initial URL's host against embeddable_host in topic_retriever.rb, but open-uri will follow redirects to any destination without re-checking. This is a real SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) vulnerability - the approved host check can be bypassed via redirect, allowing access to internal services.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39 — The test still expects synchronous TopicRetriever construction even though the controller now enqueues RetrieveTopic, so this spec will fail and does not verify the queued job payload.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for embed_controller.rb, when topic_id is nil, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, in the test spec at line 39-44, it expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. This test is checking for synchronous TopicRetriever instantiation, but the actual controller code enqueues a job instead. The test will fail because TopicRetriever.new is never called directly in the controller - instead Jobs.enqueue is called. This is a real test/implementation mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14 — PollFeed coverage only mocks poll_feed and never exercises RSS item URL/content fallbacks or TopicEmbed.import, leaving the new ingestion behavior and common malformed-feed cases unverified.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the execute method's guard conditions (checking if feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url, and embed_by_username are set) and mocks poll_feed. The actual poll_feed method in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb contains logic for parsing RSS items, handling URL fallbacks (i.e., using i.id if i.link is blank or doesn't match URL pattern), and calling TopicEmbed.import. However, this is a test coverage concern/suggestion rather than a bug in the production code. The production code in poll_feed.rb may work correctly - the finding is about test coverage being insufficient, not about actual bugs in the implementation. Test coverage suggestions are typically considered style/quality nits rather than 'real problems' in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — TopicRetriever tests stub its own internal methods instead of exercising Redis throttling and the feed-to-HTTP fallback, so regressions in the actual retrieval workflow can pass.

adjudication.rationale: The finding criticizes the test design in topic_retriever_spec.rb, noting that tests stub internal methods like `retrieved_recently?` and `perform_retrieve` instead of testing the actual Redis throttling and feed-to-HTTP fallback logic. Looking at the test code, it does indeed stub these methods (e.g., `topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve).once` and `topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false)`). However, this is a test design/quality concern rather than a bug or defect in the production code. The tests verify the conditional logic flow (when to call perform_retrieve based on host validity and throttling), which is a valid testing approach. While integration tests would provide more coverage, the current unit tests are not incorrect - they test the intended behavior at the unit level. This is a style/design opinion about test coverage, not a real bug or defect.
